title: Schengen short-stay visa (type C)
destination_description: 29 European countries, including France, Germany, Italy and Spain
visa_description: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period, for tourism, family visits, business or a short course.
source: Harmonised Schengen visa application form, Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Visa Code), Annex I

questions.prompt: Which Schengen country is your main destination?
questions.help: The country where you'll spend the most nights. If it's a tie, the one you enter first. That country's embassy handles your application.

questions.prompt: What's the main purpose of your trip?
Will you stay in the Schengen area for more than 90 days in any 180-day period?
questions.help: Count every day you'll be anywhere in the Schengen area, including the days you arrive and leave.

stop_if.message: A short-stay visa covers at most 90 days in any 180-day period. A longer stay needs a national (type D) visa from your destination country, which Ta'asheera can't prepare yet.

questions.prompt: Let's add your passport. You can upload a photo of its details page and confirm what we read, or type the details yourself.
When was your passport issued?
questions.help: It's printed on the details page, usually next to the expiry date.

rules.message: The issue date can't be in the future.
Schengen countries need a passport issued in the last 10 years. You may need to renew it first.

questions.prompt: Did you have a different surname at birth? If so, what was it?
questions.help: Leave this empty if your surname hasn't changed.

questions.prompt: Which city or town were you born in?
And which country is that in?
What's your marital status?
What's your home address?
What phone number can the embassy reach you on?
questions.help: Include the country code, for example +961 71 123 456.

questions.prompt: What do you currently do?
What's your job title?
questions.help: As your employer would write it, for example Accountant or Software engineer. It goes in the form's occupation field.

questions.prompt: What's the name of your employer or business?
Which school or university do you attend?
When do you plan to arrive in the Schengen area?

rules.message: Your arrival date needs to be in the future.
You can apply at most six months before your trip. Come back closer to the date.

questions.prompt: And when will you leave?

rules.message: You can't leave before you arrive.
A short-stay visa covers at most 90 days, counting the days you arrive and leave.
Your passport must stay valid for at least three months after you leave the Schengen area.

questions.prompt: How many times will you enter the Schengen area on this trip?
Where will you stay?
What's the name and address of the place you're staying?
Who's hosting you? Give their full name and address.
Who's paying for the trip?
Who's your sponsor, and how are they related to you?
Have your fingerprints been taken for a Schengen visa application in the last 59 months?
Roughly when were they taken?
questions.help: If you have the visa sticker, its issue date is close enough.

rules.message: That date can't be in the future.
Only fingerprints from the last 59 months count. Answer no to the previous question instead.

documents.label: Passport photo
documents.help: A recent colour photo, 35 x 45 mm, on a plain light background, taken in the last six months.

documents.label: Travel medical insurance
documents.help: Valid in every Schengen country for your whole stay, covering at least EUR 30,000 of medical costs and repatriation.

documents.label: Flight reservation
documents.help: A return or onward booking showing your entry and exit dates. A reservation is enough; you don't need to buy the ticket yet.

documents.label: Accommodation booking
documents.help: Hotel or rental bookings covering every night of the trip.

documents.label: Invitation from your host
documents.help: A letter from the person you'll stay with, with their address and a copy of their ID or residence permit.

documents.label: Bank statements
documents.help: Your last three months of statements, stamped or signed by the bank, showing you can pay for the trip.

documents.label: Sponsor's letter and bank statements
documents.help: A signed letter saying they'll pay for your trip, with their last three months of bank statements.

documents.label: Letter from your employer
documents.help: On company letterhead: your role, salary, how long you've worked there and the leave approved for the trip.

documents.label: Business registration
documents.help: Your commercial register entry or trade licence, and recent tax returns.

documents.label: Proof of enrolment
documents.help: A letter from your school or university confirming you're enrolled and allowed to travel.

documents.label: Pension statements
documents.help: Your last three months of pension payments.

documents.label: Cover letter
documents.help: A short signed letter explaining the purpose of your trip and your plans. Optional, but many consulates expect one.
